title: Eating out with friends
goal: Order street food and restaurant food for a group, say what you feel like, complain that it's too spicy or not salty enough, and sort out the bill — or insist it's your treat.
intro:
Gujaratis are famous for loving food, and eating out with friends is the centre of social life: a plate of **પાણીપૂરી** at a **લારી**, **દાબેલી** after college, **ફાફડા** on a Sunday morning, a late-night trip to Manek Chowk. This unit gives you the street names of the food, the way to order for a whole table, and the endless negotiations about **તીખું** (spicy) and **મોળું** (bland).

The grammar is all about amounts — **બહુ**, **વધારે પડતું** 'too much', **ઓછું** 'not enough', **પૂરતું** 'enough', **થોડું વધારે** 'a bit more' — and about cravings: **મને પાણીપૂરી ખાવાનું મન થાય છે** 'I feel like pani puri'. And you'll learn the most important food phrase of all: **ના ના, તું રહેવા દે, હું આપું છું!** 'no no, leave it, I'm paying!'

grammar.title: Too, not enough, enough, a little: બહુ, વધારે પડતું, ઓછું, પૂરતું, થોડું
grammar.body:
**Too / very**: **બહુ** means both 'very' and 'too'; context decides: **બહુ તીખું** 'very / too spicy'. To make it clearly a complaint, use **વધારે પડતું** 'excessive', which agrees like an adjective: **વધારે પડતું** તેલ (n), **વધારે પડતી** ખાંડ (f).

**Not enough**: Gujarati simply says 'X is less': **મીઠું ઓછું છે** 'there isn't enough salt', **ચટણી ઓછી છે** 'not enough chutney'. The opposite is **વધારે છે** 'there's too much'.

**Enough**: **પૂરતું** agrees with the thing: **પૂરતા** પૈસા, **પૂરતી** જગ્યા. When serving or ordering, people just say **બસ!** 'enough!' or **આટલું બસ છે** 'this much is enough'.

**A little more / less**: **થોડું વધારે**, **થોડું ઓછું**; **જરા** softens anything.

**So … that I can't**: **એટલું … કે** + the 'can't be done' form **-આતું નથી**: **એટલું તીખું છે કે ખવાતું નથી** 'it's so spicy I can't eat it'.

The trap: English 'too' meaning 'also' is **પણ**, not બહુ.

grammar.title: I feel like…: મને … -વાનું મન થાય છે
grammar.body:
A craving is something that **happens to you**, so the person goes in the dative (**મને, તને, એને**, like **મને ભૂખ લાગી છે**), the activity goes in the **-વાનું** form, and **મન** 'mind, heart' is the subject:

**મને + X + -વાનું મન થાય છે** 'I feel like X-ing'
**મને પાણીપૂરી ખાવાનું મન થાય છે** 'I feel like having pani puri'

**Asking**: **તને શું ખાવાનું મન છે?** 'what do you feel like eating?' (**મન છે** and **મન થાય છે** are both used.)
**Not in the mood**: **મને કંઈ ખાવાનું મન નથી** 'I don't feel like eating anything'.
**Past**: **મન થયું** 'I felt like': ગઈકાલે દાબેલી ખાવાનું મન થયું.

Compare: **મારે ખાવું છે** 'I want to eat' (a plan or decision, unit 17) and **મૂડ છે** (unit 21) 'I'm in the mood'. **મન થાય છે** is the sudden craving.

The trap: the person is **મને**, not **હું**: never ~~હું મન થાય છે~~. And the -વાનું ending stays neuter whatever the food: પાણીપૂરી ખાવા**નું** મન.

culture: Most Gujaratis are vegetarian, and many are Jain, so menus everywhere offer **જૈન** versions without onion, garlic or root vegetables — just ask **જૈન મળશે?** Gujarati home food leans slightly sweet (a little jaggery in the dal), but street food is properly spicy, so **તીખું ઓછું** is a phrase worth knowing. At a pani puri cart you stand in a circle while the **પાણીપૂરીવાળા** hands each person one puri at a time, and you're entitled to a free **સૂકી પૂરી** (a dry, filled puri) at the end. Ahmedabad's Manek Chowk is a jewellery market by day and a food market until late at night; Surat is proverbially the city of food lovers; and in the diaspora, Leicester's Belgrave Road, Wembley and Edison, New Jersey are where you'll hear Gujarati spoken over a plate of dhokla. Paying is a contest: everyone grabs for the bill with **ના ના, રહેવા દે!**, and an elder or the person with good news usually wins — **ટ્રીટ આપ!** is what friends say when you get a job, a promotion or a new car. Among students and young colleagues, splitting the bill by UPI is now completely normal.

tip.title: Ordering at a cart
tip.body:
- Order by the plate: **બે પ્લેટ** પાણીપૂરી, **એક** દાબેલી, **બે** કટિંગ.
- **આપો** is fine at a cart; **આપજો** is softer.
- **ઢોકળાં** and **ભજિયાં** are neuter plurals: ભજિયાં ઠંડાં **થઈ ગયાં**.
- **ગરમાગરમ** 'piping hot' is the best compliment for fried food.

lessons.title: What do you feel like?

tip.title: મને … ખાવાનું મન થાય છે
tip.body:
- A craving happens to you: **મને** + food + **ખાવાનું મન થાય છે** 'I feel like…'.
- Ask: **તને શું ખાવાનું મન છે?** Not in the mood: **મન નથી**.
- The person is **મને / તને / એને**, never હું.
- Past: **મન થયું**.

tip.title: Ordering politely
tip.body:
- In a restaurant ask with **-શો?**: મેનુ **આપશો?**, પૅક કરી **આપશો?**
- **X વગર** 'without X': ડુંગળી **વગર**. **જૈન** = no onion, garlic or root vegetables.
- **એક-એક** 'one each'.
- 'Have you ordered?' is ergative and agrees with ઑર્ડર (m): ઑર્ડર **આપ્યો**?

sentences.en: Can I get it Jain? Without onion and garlic.

sentences.en: No onion for me, please.

sentences.native: બધા માટે એક-એક છાશ લાવજો.
sentences.roman: badhā māṭe ek-ek chhāsh lāvjo.
sentences.en: Bring a buttermilk for everyone, please.

sentences.native: ઑર્ડર આપી દીધો?
sentences.roman: orḍar āpī dīdho?
sentences.en: Have you ordered already?

sentences.native: અમે હજી ઑર્ડર નથી આપ્યો.
sentences.roman: ame hajī orḍar nathī āpyo.
sentences.en: We haven't ordered yet.

sentences.native: આ પૅક કરી આપશો? ઘરે લઈ જવું છે.
sentences.roman: ā pek karī āpsho? ghare laī javuṃ chhe.
sentences.en: Could you pack this up? I want to take it home.

sentences.native: બાકીનું પૅક કરી દો.
sentences.roman: bākīnuṃ pek karī do.
sentences.en: Pack up the rest.

sentences.native: એ લસણ નથી ખાતી, એ જૈન છે.
sentences.roman: e lasaṇ nathī khātī, e jain chhe.
sentences.en: She doesn't eat garlic, she's Jain.

tip.title: Too much, not enough, enough
tip.body:
- **બહુ** = very / too. A clear complaint: **વધારે પડતું** (agrees: વધારે પડતી ખાંડ).
- 'Not enough X' = **X ઓછું છે**: મીઠું **ઓછું** છે.
- **પૂરતું** 'enough' agrees: ચટણી **પૂરતી** નથી.
- **થોડું વધારે** 'a bit more' · **બસ!** 'that's enough!'
tip.pattern: X ઓછું / વધારે / વધારે પડતું / પૂરતું છે

sentences.native: તીખું ઓછું રાખજો, મારો મિત્ર લંડનથી આવ્યો છે.
sentences.roman: tīkhuṃ ochhuṃ rākhjo, māro mitra laṇḍanthī āvyo chhe.
sentences.en: Go easy on the chilli, my friend's come from London.

sentences.native: આ તો બહુ તીખું છે! પાણી આપજો.
sentences.roman: ā to bahu tīkhuṃ chhe! pāṇī āpjo.
sentences.en: This is way too spicy! Some water, please.

sentences.native: મીઠું ઓછું છે, થોડું આપશો?
sentences.roman: mīṭhuṃ ochhuṃ chhe, thoḍuṃ āpsho?
sentences.en: It needs salt, could I have a little?

sentences.native: ભજિયાંમાં વધારે પડતું તેલ છે.
sentences.roman: bhajiyāṃmāṃ vadhāre paḍtuṃ tel chhe.
sentences.en: The bhajiya are far too oily.

sentences.native: ચામાં ખાંડ વધારે પડતી છે.
sentences.roman: chāmāṃ khāṃḍ vadhāre paḍtī chhe.
sentences.en: The tea is far too sweet.

sentences.native: આ દાળ બહુ મોળી છે, થોડો મસાલો આપો.
sentences.roman: ā dāḷ bahu moḷī chhe, thoḍo masālo āpo.
sentences.en: This dal is really bland, give me a bit of spice.

sentences.native: ચટણી પૂરતી નથી, થોડી વધારે આપજો.
sentences.roman: chaṭṇī pūrtī nathī, thoḍī vadhāre āpjo.
sentences.en: There isn't enough chutney, a bit more please.

sentences.native: ચાર જણ માટે પૂરતું ખાવાનું છે?
sentences.roman: chār jaṇ māṭe pūrtuṃ khāvānuṃ chhe?
sentences.en: Is there enough food for four people?

sentences.native: એટલું તીખું છે કે ખવાતું નથી!
sentences.roman: eṭluṃ tīkhuṃ chhe ke khavātuṃ nathī!
sentences.en: It's so spicy I can't eat it!

sentences.native: બસ, પેટ ભરાઈ ગયું. હવે કંઈ નહીં.
sentences.roman: bas, peṭ bharāī gayuṃ. have kaṃī nahīṃ.
sentences.en: That's it, I'm full. Nothing more now.

lessons.title: Paying the bill

tip.title: Who pays?
tip.body:
- Ask for it: **બિલ લાવજો**.
- Everyone fights to pay: **ના ના, તું રહેવા દે!** (to elders **રહેવા દો**).
- **મારા તરફથી** 'on me' · **ટ્રીટ આપવી** 'to treat everyone' — ટ્રીટ is feminine: ટ્રીટ **આપી**.
- Split it: **બિલ વહેંચી લઈએ**.

new: ના ના, તું રહેવા દે, હું આપું છું.

sentences.native: ભાઈ, બિલ લાવજો.
sentences.roman: bhāī, bil lāvjo.
sentences.en: Bhai, the bill, please.

sentences.native: આજે મારા તરફથી! મને નોકરી મળી ગઈ.
sentences.roman: āje mārā tarafthī! mane nokrī maḷī gaī.
sentences.en: It's on me today! I got the job.

sentences.native: નવી નોકરી? તો ટ્રીટ આપવી પડશે!
sentences.roman: navī nokrī? to ṭrīṭ āpvī paḍshe!
sentences.en: A new job? Then you'll have to treat us!

sentences.native: બિલ વહેંચી લઈએ, બધા ઑનલાઇન આપી દો.
sentences.roman: bil vaheṃchī laīe, badhā onlāin āpī do.
sentences.en: Let's split the bill, everyone pay online.

sentences.native: ના ના, તું રહેવા દે, હું આપું છું.
sentences.roman: nā nā, tuṃ rahevā de, huṃ āpuṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: No, no, leave it, I'm paying.

sentences.native: ગઈ વખતે તેં બિલ આપ્યું હતું, આજે હું આપીશ.
sentences.roman: gaī vakhate teṃ bil āpyuṃ hatuṃ, āje huṃ āpīsh.
sentences.en: You paid last time, today I'll pay.

sentences.native: પૈસા ઑનલાઇન મોકલી દઉં?
sentences.roman: paisā onlāin moklī dauṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I send you the money online?

sentences.native: એણે બધાને ટ્રીટ આપી.
sentences.roman: eṇe badhāne ṭrīṭ āpī.
sentences.en: He treated everyone.

sentences.native: રહેવા દો, કાકા, આજે અમારા તરફથી.
sentences.roman: rahevā do, kākā, āje amārā tarafthī.
sentences.en: Leave it, uncle, today it's on us.
